manifest.name: Expenses
manifest.summary: Submit, validate and reinvoice employee expenses

behavioral_notes.element: hr.expense state machine (action_submit / action_approve / action_post / action_reset)
behavioral_notes.observation: The expense lifecycle is driven by approval_state ('submitted'/'approved'/'refused') and the computed state (draft -> submitted -> approved -> posted -> in_payment -> paid; refused is terminal). action_submit sets approval_state='submitted' (or auto-validates via _can_be_autovalidated when there is no approver) and schedules the 'Review this expense' activity on the manager; action_approve runs _check_can_approve, validates analytic distribution, pops a duplicate-confirmation wizard if duplicate_expense_ids overlap, then _do_approve writes approval_state='approved'. state is recomputed (not directly written) from the linked account_move_id's state/payment_state. Not visible in metadata; lives in models/hr_expense.py.

Posting bridges HR into accounting. Employee-paid ('own_account') expenses go through hr.expense.post.wizard and _post_without_wizard, which groups by employee and creates an in_receipt account.move (vendor receipt) on the purchase/expense journal via _prepare_receipts_vals + _prepare_move_lines_vals, then action_post. Company-paid ('company_account') expenses call _create_company_paid_moves, which creates an account.move plus a linked account.payment (origin_payment_id) and posts the payment. account_move_id is stored back on the expense; reset (action_reset) reverses or unlinks the move. This account.move/account.payment creation is invisible in metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: hr.expense analytic_distribution (analytic.mixin) -> re-invoice to sale.order via expense_policy (sale_expense bridge)
behavioral_notes.observation: hr.expense inherits analytic.mixin; _compute_analytic_distribution derives a distribution from account.analytic.distribution.model (by product/category/partner/account-prefix). Each posted move line carries this analytic_distribution, producing an account.analytic.line — the value-link spine. The base module stops at accounting. The auto-installed bridge sale_expense (depends sale_management+hr_expense) adds sale_order_id + can_be_reinvoiced on hr.expense, keyed off product.template.expense_policy (defined in sale: 'no'/'cost'/'sales_price'). On posting, sale_expense.action_post creates/sets the SO's analytic account; account.move.line._sale_can_be_reinvoice() + _sale_create_reinvoice_sale_line() then push the analytic line onto a new sale.order.line (qty_delivered), re-invoicing the cost to the customer. Confirms PRIMARY_SUPPORT_INTEGRATION_AR.md link #4 (المصاريف -> الخدمة).

behavioral_notes.element: hr.expense mail alias intake (message_new) + duplicate/same-receipt detection
behavioral_notes.observation: Expenses can be created by email: message_new resolves the sender to an hr.employee (_get_employee_from_email) and parses the subject for product code, price and currency (_parse_expense_subject), creating a draft expense and replying with a confirmation mail. _compute_duplicate_expense_ids runs a raw SQL self-join (employee+product+date+amount+company+currency) and _compute_same_receipt_expense_ids groups attachments by checksum to surface possible duplicates before approval. None of this is derivable from field/model metadata.

11 JS files, 5 XML templates, 3 OWL components (ExpenseDashboard, AttachmentNumber, QRModalComponent), 7 registry registrations (nb_attachment field widget; dashboard/kanban/tree/form view overrides; hr_expense_tour), 2 patches (ActivityMenu.prototype, AttachmentView.prototype). Asset bundles: web.assets_backend (8), web.assets_tests (2), web.report_assets_common (1). Not in Python metadata.

information_flows: side-effect: hr.expense.action_post -> account.move (in_receipt) for employee-paid; account.move + account.payment for company-paid
side-effect: posted move lines carry analytic_distribution -> account.analytic.line (cost spine)
bridge (sale_expense, auto_install): expense_policy on product + sale_order_id -> account.move.line._sale_create_reinvoice_sale_line -> sale.order.line (re-invoice to customer)
intake: mail alias message_new -> draft hr.expense from email subject

capabilities: Capture & Submit Employee Expenses (incl. email/receipt intake)
Post Expenses to Accounting (employee reimbursement & company-paid)
Re-invoice Expenses to Customers (via expense_policy, sale_expense bridge)
value_streams: Expense-to-Reimburse: draft -> submitted -> approved -> posted (account.move) -> in_payment -> paid
Expense-to-Cash (re-invoice): approved expense -> analytic line -> sale.order.line -> customer invoice (with sale_expense)
policies: 12 record rules: employee sees own expenses, approvers see team/department, multi-company scoping
Approval gate: only 'approved' expenses can be posted (_check_can_create_move); posted/approved expenses cannot be deleted
Auto-validation when employee has no approver (_can_be_autovalidated); duplicate-receipt warning before approval
metrics: Expense dashboard (To Submit / Waiting Approval / Waiting Reimbursement amounts)

classification.rationale: hr_expense is a support activity (Stabell & Fjeldstad: an infrastructure/HR-administration function), not a primary value-creating step. Its home is HR — category 'Human Resources/Expenses', owned by HR approver groups, operating on hr.employee — so the primary APQC fit is 7.0 Develop and Manage Human Capital (reward/reimburse employees: submit-approve-reimburse expenses). It is a bridge: every posted expense feeds 9.0 Finance (creates account.move / account.payment, the AP/reimbursement leg) via its hard dependency on account, and through the auto-installed sale_expense bridge (expense_policy + sale_order_id) it can re-invoice costs into 3.0 Market and Sell / sale.order, charging the customer. The analytic_distribution it carries is the cost spine that lands these support costs onto the analytic account (value unit) for margin. Chosen 7.0 over 9.0 because ownership, security and the employee-facing lifecycle are HR; Finance and Sales are downstream consumers it feeds, not its owning activity.

standard_capabilities: Expense capture (manual, email alias, attachment/receipt upload)
Multi-level approval workflow with refuse-reason and duplicate detection
Employee-paid reimbursement and company-paid (card) posting to accounting
Expense split wizard and analytic distribution
Re-invoice to customer via product expense_policy (with sale_expense)
typical_fits: Standard submit/approve/reimburse flow for employee expenses
Company credit-card expenses logged and reconciled via account.payment
Billable travel/expense re-invoiced to a confirmed sales order
Approver hierarchy via expense_manager_id / department manager / team leader
common_gaps: Per-category or per-amount spending policies / mileage & per-diem rules (need config or extra apps)
Multi-step / threshold-based approval chains beyond the single approver model

open_questions: Exact recompute order of the ~15 monetary/tax compute methods (total_amount vs tax_amount vs currency_rate) when a custom rate is set.
Behavior of company-paid vs employee-paid posting when batching expenses across journals/payment methods.
Whether re-invoicing is in scope for this deployment (requires the auto-installed sale_expense bridge + product expense_policy configured).
